4. The prosecution examined as many as 14 witnesses in support of the prosecution case and the defence examined only one witness of the witnesses so examined by the prosecution. PW 1 Nabakumar Das is the informant who lodged the FIR, PW 5 Constable No. 42 Abdur Rashid laid ambush near at the Noor Mahal cinema hall in order to apprehend accused Bashna, PW 6 Constable No. 8 Abdul Gafar has been tendered and the defence declined to cross-examine him, PW 9 Mizanur Rahman also laid ambush near at the Noor Mahal cinema hall in order to apprehend accused Bazlur Rahman @ Bashna, PW 12 Md. Ejarat Ali, Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police filled in the form of the First Information Report. PW 13 Md. Abdul Kafi Miah is the Chemical Examiner who examined the parcel sent to him for the Chemical Examination. PW 14 Md. Mozibor Rahman, Inspector of Police, cm Camp Rangpur proved the sketch map with index and also stated that sketch map was prepared by Ali Asraf, Sub-Inspector of Police and he knows his signature. He stated that Ali Asraf the Investigation Officer in his diary mentioned that he examined the father-in-law of accused Kazal. The prosecution also examined the seizure-list witnesses such as Abdul Majid, Razaul Alam, Sultan Mahmud, Haider Ali, Afzal Hussain and Mokbul Hossain. It is the case of the prosecution that on the admission of accused Bazlur Rahman @ Bashna they recovered the incriminating heroin from the possession of the accused. Section 25 of the Evidence Act says that confession or admission made to the police officer should not be proved and section 26 further says that confession or admission made by an accused while he is in police custody should not be proved against such accused but so much of the information received by the police while the accused made such confession or admission or the accused made such confession or admission while he was in custody of the police could only be received in evidence if such information leads to the discovery of incriminating articles. In this case the prosecution alleges that Bazlur Rahman @ Bashna admitted to the police while he was arrested or in police custody that certain amount of heroin was in possession of accused Zulfikar Ali @ Kazal and in pursuance of such information, police raided the house of Kazal and recovered the incriminating articles. If no such articles were recovered then this admission or confession cannot be admitted into evidence. 

 5. Let us now examine if any such heroin was at all recovered from the possession of accused Bashna and Kazal. Section 102 CrPC relates to search or inspection and section 103 relates to manner and method in which such searches are to be made. Section 103 provided that the officer or other person who makes the search shall call upon two or more respectable inhabitants of the locality to attend and witness the search. Search shall be made in their presence and a list of all things seized in the course of such search and of the places in which they are respectively found shall be prepared by such officer or other persons and signed by such witnesses but no person witnessing a search under this section shall be required to attend the Court as a witness of the search unless specially summoned by it. The occupant of the place to be searched shall be permitted to attend during the search and a copy of the list prepared under this section signed by the said witnesses shall be delivered to the occupant or person at his request. When search is made under section 102(3) a list of all things taken possession of shall be prepared and a copy thereof shall be delivered to such person at his request. Any person who, without reasonable cause, refuses or neglects to attend and witness a search under this section, when called upon to do so by an order in writing delivered or tendered to him, shall be deemed to have committed an offence under section 187 of the Penal Code. 

 6. Regulation No. 280 of the Police Regulation, 1943 sets out the law in regard to search as contained in Chapter VII and sections 102 and 103, 165 and 166 of Code of Criminal Procedure. These sections must be scrupulously followed. The officer conducting a search should take precautions to prevent the possibility, on the one hand, of any articles being introduced into the house without the knowledge of the inmates and, on the other, of any articles being taken out of the house while the search is in progress. Search should be made in the presence of the owner or someone on his behalf. The presence of search witnesses (vide clause (h) below) must not be looked upon merely as a formality, but they must actually be eye-witnesses to the whole search and must be able to see clearly where each article is found. They should then sign the search list (BP Form No. 44). If any search witness be illiterate, it should be read over to him and his left thumb impression should be taken on it. Where the witnesses do not know English, it should be written in the vernacular. The suspected person whose property is seized, should, if present at the search, also be asked to sign the list. Should he refuse, a note will be made to this' effect and it should be certified to by the witnesses. The suspected person, or in his absence, the person in charge of the house or place searched, should be given a copy of the search list. He will be given an opportunity of comparing it with the original and be asked to sign an acknowledgment for the copy of the original list. Should he refuse, a note to that effect should be made and should be certified to by witnesses. Only searches for any specific article, which is known or reasonably suspected to be in any particular place or in the possession of any particular person, can be made without warrants. General searches without warrants are illegal and the only search which can be made without warrant is under section 165, Code of Criminal Procedure. Before the commencement of the search the person of every police officer who is to conduct it, as also that of every witness and informer shall be examined before the witnesses and the owner of the house or his representative. All articles or weapons found at a house-search or on the person of a prisoner shall be carefully labeled and if a charge-sheet is submitted in the case, shall be sent to the Court officer. The labels shall be signed by the officer conducting the search. 

 8. PW 2 Md. Abdul Majid is the seizure-list witness relating to the alleged recovery of heroin from the possession of accused Zulfikar Ali @ Kazal. He stated in his evidence that on 27.10.89 someone knocked at his door at about 9-15 PM. He came out and found a constable who told him to go to the house of Rafique Mondal, father of accused Kazal. He found some police officers and other public there. One police officer showed him a packet and said that the packet was recovered from Kazal and he put his signature Ext.3/2. He was declared hostile by the prosecution. In his cross-examination he stated that before signing the paper, police told him that this packet contained heroin. In his cross-examination by the defence he stated that he did know from where the packet was found or what were the contents of such packet. 

 13. So these witnesses, namely, PWs 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8 did not prove that the incriminating article, namely, heroin was at all recovered in their presence from the house of accused Kazal. We have noticed that the laws and rules relating to search and seizure have not been followed by the police while they made the search and seized the alleged incriminating article. Non-compliance with the mandatory provisions of section 103 CrPC and the Regulation No. 280 of the Police Regulation, 1943 make the search and seizure wholly illegal, Furthermore, the above mentioned seizure-list witnesses did not say any word as to the seizure of heroin in their presence, as such, the prosecution totally failed in proving that heroin was at all seized in their presence and, by the police. Therefore the admission or confession made to police by accused Bazlur Rahman @ Bashna and Zulfikar Ali @ Kazal cannot be taken to be as evidence under sections 25 and 26 of the Evidence Act because such admission did not result in recovery of any incriminating or prohibited articles, as such, the evidence of the police witnesses do not in any way help the prosecution. 

 14. PW 13 Md. Abdul Kafi Mia, the chemical examiner, stated in his evidence that on 29.10.89 by memo No.106 was sent to the Magistrate, Kotwali Rangpur vide diary No.1618 dated 27.10.89 to examine a parcel as sent by SI Abdus Sattar to chemically examine. He stated in his evidence that 3 (three) packets were sent to him: one contained 35 gram brown colour. Another contained 35 grams of brown colour powder articles yet another contained 5.5. grams and other contained 98.5 grams brown coloured powder substance and in each of these brown coloured substance there exists heroin but the seizure list in fact discloses grey colour substance which was sent to the examiner for chemical examination but from the evidence of PW 13 it is clear that he had examined the substance of brown colour. The learned Judge observed that the colour of the contents of the packet which contains 100 grams of heroin looked gray. The said articles having been seized at night the colour might look a bit different. This observation is based on conjecture and surmises. In his cross-examination PW 13 has stated 

 Therefore the substance alleged to have been recovered from the possession of the accused has not been examined by the chemical examiner and the net result is that there is no iota of evidence that the seized goods are heroin as alleged by the prosecution. Therefore the prosecution has totally failed in proving that any substance falling within the purview of section 19(1) Kha and 19(1) Ka respectively or under section 9 of the 'Madak Drabaya Niyantran Ayen', 1990 has at all been recovered from the possession of the accused. The order of conviction is ex facie bad and is not sustainable in law and, as such, the accused-appellant Zulfikar Ali @ Kazal and Bazlar Rahman @ Bashna are found not guilty of the offence under section 19(1) Kha and 19(1) Ka of the Madak Drabaya Niyantran Ayen, 1990.
